data.cultural_impact: The name Muqatadir holds a significant cultural impact as it is a name associated with strength, resilience, and unwavering commitment. In Arab and Islamic cultures, names are often given based on the qualities the parents hope their child will embody. Muqatadir, as a name, inspires its bearer to be like the historical figure it is named after - to persist in the face of challenges and to endure through hardships.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Muqatadir holds a profound spiritual significance as it is a reminder of the importance of steadfastness and unwavering faith in Allah (swt). It is mentioned in Hadith that Muqatadir was one of the blessed companions of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), known for his unwavering belief and commitment to Allah. As such, bearing this name could serve as an ongoing reminder to the bearer to uphold their faith, and to be steadfast and unwavering in their commitment to Allah and His teachings. Furthermore, it could inspire the bearer to be a role model of resilience and steadfastness in their own lives, reflecting the virtues of this esteemed companion.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Tarikh al-Fitnah al-Kubra, p. 104 The name Muqatadir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Muqatadir bin Sulaiman al-Khuldi was given to Marwan ibn Muhammad, the Umayyad Caliph, after he assumed power by force against his father, Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik. The name Muqatadir (Persistently Firm) was given to him by the people due to his unwavering determination and refusal to back down from his claim to the caliphate.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn al-Athir, Al-Kamil fi al-Tarikh, vol. 3, p. 197 The name Muqatadir carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Abdullah ibn Tahir, the founder of the Tahirid Empire in Iran and Central Asia, was known as the 'Sword of Muqatadir'. This was a reference to Marwan ibn Muhammad, the Umayyad Caliph mentioned earlier, who was called Muqatadir due to his unyielding determination. Abdullah ibn Tahir adopted this title as a symbol of his own firmness and resolve.
